newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended slightly higher on Monday after a very quiet day, due to the Christmas and New Year holiday season.

The 6.25 July 1998 benchmark ended two basis points higher at 104.17/25, while the Sept 2001 was up 0.13 at 116.92/117.02. The Jan 2006 closed 0.10 higher than Friday at 102.22/32 and the 30-year bond was up 14 basis points at 112.76 bid.
Today was the last official trading day on the Dutch bond market, but many players had already closed their books and were taking an extended holiday.
With few players, price movements proved more volatile but were not based on fundamentals, dealers said, adding that activity was below-average in all maturities.

Stronger than expected U.S. November new housing starts, announced in the afternoon, may have been among the factors pushing Dutch bond prices down, but dealers said the thin trade also caused prices to move.
"You can no longer speak of a market, really. If you want a trade worth 25 million guilders, you suddenly get a totally different price," one said.
The market is expected to return to normal levels of trade next Monday, dealers said, noting, however, that some may be attracted back earlier.
"On Thursday, the finance ministry will start trading the issues it announced today. That will lure some players back into the market," one said.
